_comment: Claim bank for expert sourcing. Every citation here was retrieved via firecrawl_research_inspect_paper on 2026-09-14; none was written from memory. 01_source may assemble pitches ONLY from these records, hedges intact. Validated and drift-checked by pipelines/lib/claims.py.
journal_note: journal is derived from the verified DOI prefix, not returned by inspect_paper. n is the sample size stated in the returned abstract; 0 means it was not stated there and was NOT inferred.

claims.claim: In a long-running Finnish study of middle-aged men, those who used a sauna four to seven times a week had a lower rate of fatal cardiovascular events than those who went once a week.

citations.title: Association between sauna bathing and fatal cardiovascular and all-cause mortality events.
Sauna bathing is associated with reduced cardiovascular mortality and improves risk prediction in men and women: a prospective cohort study.

claims.hedge: This is an observational association in a population where sauna use is lifelong and near-universal. It does not establish that sauna use caused the difference, and people who sauna often may differ in other ways.
do_not_say: Saunas prevent heart attacks
Sauna use will extend your life
A sauna is as good as cardiovascular exercise

claims.claim: The same cohort found the association held in women as well as men when it was re-examined with both sexes included.

citations.title: Sauna bathing is associated with reduced cardiovascular mortality and improves risk prediction in men and women: a prospective cohort study.

claims.hedge: One cohort, one country, one bathing culture. It has not been replicated in a population where sauna use is occasional rather than habitual.
do_not_say: Saunas protect women from heart disease
This applies to any population

claims.claim: Frequent sauna bathing was associated with lower all-cause mortality, and the association was present across levels of cardiorespiratory fitness.

citations.title: Joint associations of sauna bathing and cardiorespiratory fitness on cardiovascular and all-cause mortality risk: a long-term prospective cohort study.
Association between sauna bathing and fatal cardiovascular and all-cause mortality events.

claims.hedge: Observational. Fitness was measured at baseline only, and unmeasured differences between frequent and infrequent bathers cannot be ruled out.
do_not_say: Sauna use adds years to your life
Sauna can substitute for being fit

claims.claim: A single sauna session lowers blood pressure for a period afterwards, with systolic pressure falling by roughly seven points in one controlled study.

citations.title: Sauna exposure leads to improved arterial compliance: Findings from a non-randomised experimental study.

claims.hedge: This is a short-term effect measured after one session, not evidence of lasting blood-pressure control.
do_not_say: Sauna treats hypertension
You can reduce or stop blood-pressure medication
Sauna replaces antihypertensives

claims.claim: Eight weeks of regular passive heat exposure improved blood-vessel function and arterial stiffness in sedentary adults in a controlled trial.

citations.title: Passive heat therapy improves endothelial function, arterial stiffness and blood pressure in sedentary humans.

claims.hedge: A small trial in young sedentary adults using hot-water immersion, not sauna, and measuring intermediate markers rather than clinical events.
do_not_say: Heat therapy reverses cardiovascular disease
Sauna unclogs arteries

claims.claim: When sauna bathing was tested as an eight-week randomised intervention in adults who already had coronary artery disease, it did not produce the vascular improvements seen in healthy sedentary people.

citations.title: Finnish sauna bathing and vascular health of adults with coronary artery disease: a randomized controlled trial.
Passive heat therapy improves endothelial function, arterial stiffness and blood pressure in sedentary humans.

claims.hedge: A null result in an established-disease population. It does not negate the observational mortality findings, but it does show the benefit is not automatic in patients.
do_not_say: Sauna is proven therapy for heart patients
Heart patients should use sauna to treat their disease

claims.claim: In the same Finnish cohort, more frequent sauna bathing was associated with a lower recorded rate of dementia and Alzheimer's disease.

citations.title: Sauna bathing is inversely associated with dementia and Alzheimer's disease in middle-aged Finnish men.

claims.hedge: Observational, men only, and dementia diagnosis in a cohort of this era is imprecise. Reverse causation is plausible: early cognitive decline may reduce sauna use rather than the reverse.
do_not_say: Saunas prevent dementia
Sauna protects the brain
Sauna reduces Alzheimer's risk

claims.claim: Warming the body one to two hours before bed shortens the time it takes to fall asleep, by about ten minutes on average across the pooled trials.

citations.title: Before-bedtime passive body heating by warm shower or bath to improve sleep: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

claims.hedge: The pooled evidence is for warm baths and showers, not saunas, and timing matters — the effect depends on heating well before bed rather than immediately before.
do_not_say: Sauna cures insomnia
A sauna before bed guarantees better sleep
Heat is a treatment for sleep disorders

claims.claim: Passive body heating in the evening increased slow-wave sleep in a small study of older women with insomnia.

citations.title: Effects of passive body heating on the sleep of older female insomniacs.
citations.journal: Journal of Geriatric Psychiatry and Neurology

citations.title: Before-bedtime passive body heating by warm shower or bath to improve sleep: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

claims.hedge: Nine participants, one small crossover study from 1996. This is early and narrow evidence, not an established effect.
do_not_say: Heat increases deep sleep
Sauna improves sleep architecture
Proven to increase slow-wave sleep

claims.claim: Repeated passive heat exposure raises intracellular heat shock protein 70, one of the cellular stress responses also triggered by exercise.

citations.title: Heat acclimation-induced intracellular HSP70 in humans: a meta-analysis.

claims.hedge: This is a cellular marker, not a health outcome. Nobody has shown that raising HSP70 by heating produces a clinical benefit in humans.
do_not_say: Sauna triggers cellular repair that prevents disease
Heat shock proteins are why sauna extends lifespan
Sauna gives you the benefits of exercise

claims.claim: A single session of passive heating produces a measurable inflammatory and heat shock protein response broadly similar in direction to moderate exercise.

citations.title: The effect of passive heating on heat shock protein 70 and interleukin-6: A possible treatment tool for metabolic diseases?

claims.hedge: Small mechanistic study measuring blood markers over hours. Similar direction is not equivalent magnitude, and no outcome was measured.
do_not_say: A sauna session equals a workout
Sauna is exercise for people who cannot exercise
Passive heating replaces physical activity

claims.claim: Cold exposure activates brown adipose tissue in adults, which increases energy expenditure while the cold lasts.

citations.title: Metabolic Effects of Brown Adipose Tissue Activity Due to Cold Exposure in Humans: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of RCTs and Non-RCTs.

claims.hedge: Brown fat activation is measured in laboratory conditions over short exposures. The energy involved is small and has not been shown to produce meaningful weight change.
do_not_say: Cold plunging burns fat
Cold exposure is a weight-loss tool
Brown fat activation will make you leaner

claims.claim: In a study of men, cold-induced brown fat activity was accompanied by changes in plasma fatty acids and measures of glucose metabolism.

citations.title: Cold-Induced Brown Adipose Tissue Activity Alters Plasma Fatty Acids and Improves Glucose Metabolism in Men.
citations.journal: The Journal of Clinical Endocrinology and Metabolism

citations.title: Metabolic Effects of Brown Adipose Tissue Activity Due to Cold Exposure in Humans: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of RCTs and Non-RCTs.

claims.hedge: Small, male-only, short-duration, and measuring biochemical markers rather than diabetes risk or any clinical endpoint.
do_not_say: Cold plunges improve insulin sensitivity
Cold exposure helps manage blood sugar
Cold plunging prevents diabetes

claims.claim: Across the pooled trials, cold-water immersion is followed by a short-lived improvement in self-reported mood and wellbeing.

citations.title: Effects of cold-water immersion on health and wellbeing: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

claims.hedge: Effects in the pooled data are short-lived, measured mostly in healthy volunteers, and self-reported in studies that cannot be blinded — people know they got in cold water.
do_not_say: Cold plunging treats depression
Cold water is an antidepressant
Cold exposure fixes anxiety

claims.claim: A short cold-water immersion increased positive affect in a small imaging study, alongside changes in connectivity between brain networks.

citations.title: Short-Term Head-Out Whole-Body Cold-Water Immersion Facilitates Positive Affect and Increases Interaction between Large-Scale Brain Networks.
Effects of cold-water immersion on health and wellbeing: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

claims.hedge: A small first-of-its-kind imaging study. Brain-network changes are not evidence of therapeutic benefit.
do_not_say: Cold plunging rewires your brain
Cold exposure changes brain function for the better
Neuroscience proves cold plunging works

claims.claim: A single session of whole-body hyperthermia reduced depressive symptoms compared with a sham procedure in a randomised trial of adults with major depressive disorder.

citations.title: Whole-Body Hyperthermia for the Treatment of Major Depressive Disorder: A Randomized Clinical Trial.

claims.hedge: One small trial, in a clinical population, using medically supervised whole-body hyperthermia under controlled conditions — not a domestic sauna, and not repeated dosing.
do_not_say: Saunas treat depression
Sauna is an antidepressant
Heat therapy is proven for mental health
Use a sauna instead of medication

claims.claim: Cold-water immersion after hard exercise reduces muscle soreness in the days that follow.

citations.title: Effects of Cold Water Immersion and Contrast Water Therapy for Recovery From Team Sport: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
citations.journal: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research

citations.title: Contrast water therapy and exercise induced muscle damage: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

claims.hedge: The reliable effect is on perceived soreness. Effects on actual performance recovery are smaller and less consistent across studies.
do_not_say: Cold plunging speeds healing
Cold immersion repairs muscle damage
Ice baths make you recover faster

claims.claim: Regular cold-water immersion straight after strength training blunts muscle growth compared with passive recovery.

citations.title: Post-exercise cold water immersion attenuates acute anabolic signalling and long-term adaptations in muscle to strength training.
Cold water immersion attenuates anabolic signaling and skeletal muscle fiber hypertrophy, but not strength gain, following whole-body resistance training.

claims.hedge: This is the trade-off that matters for anyone lifting weights: the same cold that reduces soreness also attenuates the adaptation. Strength gains appear less affected than muscle size.
do_not_say: Cold plunging is bad for you
Never use cold water after exercise
Cold immersion causes muscle loss

claims.claim: Because cold immersion interferes with the muscle-building response, timing it away from strength sessions is the practical way to keep the soreness benefit without the trade-off.

citations.title: Cold water immersion attenuates anabolic signaling and skeletal muscle fiber hypertrophy, but not strength gain, following whole-body resistance training.
Post-exercise cold water immersion attenuates acute anabolic signalling and long-term adaptations in muscle to strength training.

claims.hedge: A reasonable inference from the trial evidence on timing and adaptation, not a protocol that has itself been tested head to head.
do_not_say: The optimal cold plunge protocol is proven
Science says plunge X hours after training

claims.claim: Alternating hot and cold water after exercise reduces muscle soreness, performing comparably to cold-water immersion alone in pooled trials.

citations.title: Contrast water therapy and exercise induced muscle damage: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Effects of Cold Water Immersion and Contrast Water Therapy for Recovery From Team Sport: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
citations.journal: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research

claims.hedge: Pooled from small studies with varied protocols. There is no established optimal ratio of hot to cold, and contrast therapy has not been shown to beat cold alone.
do_not_say: Contrast therapy is the best recovery method
Hot-cold cycling flushes toxins
Contrast therapy boosts circulation to heal injury

claims.claim: Sweat loss in a sauna typically runs around 0.6 to 1 kilogram per hour, which is why fluid replacement matters more than most people assume.

citations.title: Human thermoregulation in sauna.
Sauna-induced body mass loss in young sedentary women and men.

claims.hedge: Rates vary substantially with body size, heat tolerance and session length. These are typical figures, not a prescription.
do_not_say: Sauna detoxifies the body through sweat
Sweating removes heavy metals or toxins

claims.claim: Weight lost during a sauna session is fluid, and it returns as soon as you rehydrate.

citations.title: Sauna-induced body mass loss in young sedentary women and men.
Human thermoregulation in sauna.

claims.hedge: Body-mass loss in a sauna is water, not fat. Treating it as fat loss is the most common misreading of the scale after a session.
do_not_say: Saunas burn fat
You can lose weight in a sauna
Sauna is a weight-loss tool
A sauna session burns X calories of fat

claims.claim: Sauna bathing is not advised for people with unstable angina, a recent heart attack, or severe aortic stenosis.

citations.title: Benefits and risks of sauna bathing.

claims.hedge: These are the established contraindications. Anyone with a cardiac diagnosis should ask their own physician rather than rely on a general rule.
do_not_say: Sauna is dangerous for heart patients generally
People with heart disease must avoid saunas

claims.claim: For most people with stable coronary heart disease, sauna bathing is generally well tolerated.

citations.title: Benefits and risks of sauna bathing.
Finnish sauna bathing and vascular health of adults with coronary artery disease: a randomized controlled trial.

claims.hedge: Well tolerated is not the same as beneficial — the randomised trial in coronary artery disease found no vascular improvement. Individual clearance still comes from the treating clinician.
do_not_say: Sauna is safe for everyone with heart disease
Sauna treats coronary disease
Heart patients should sauna for their condition

claims.claim: Alcohol and sauna are a genuinely dangerous combination, and alcohol is implicated in a large share of sauna-related deaths.

citations.title: Sauna deaths in Sweden, 1992-2003.
citations.journal: The American Journal of Forensic Medicine and Pathology

citations.title: Alcohol and sauna bathing: effects on cardiac rhythm, blood pressure, and serum electrolyte and cortisol concentrations.

claims.hedge: In the Swedish forensic series, alcohol was involved in roughly 44 per cent of the deaths examined. Bathing alone compounds the risk.
do_not_say: Sauna is dangerous
A drink before the sauna is fine in moderation

claims.claim: Combining alcohol with sauna heat raises the risk of cardiac rhythm disturbance, with the hangover phase carrying particular risk.

citations.title: Alcohol and sauna bathing: effects on cardiac rhythm, blood pressure, and serum electrolyte and cortisol concentrations.
Sauna deaths in Sweden, 1992-2003.
citations.journal: The American Journal of Forensic Medicine and Pathology

claims.hedge: Demonstrated in a small controlled study of ten healthy men plus forensic case data, not a large clinical trial.
do_not_say: Sauna causes arrhythmia
Sauna is unsafe for anyone with palpitations

claims.claim: Bathing alone is a recurring feature of fatal sauna incidents, which is a practical argument for not using a home sauna alone after drinking.

citations.title: Sauna deaths in Sweden, 1992-2003.
citations.journal: The American Journal of Forensic Medicine and Pathology

claims.hedge: Drawn from a forensic case series, which describes deaths that occurred and cannot give a rate of risk for ordinary use.
do_not_say: Never use a sauna alone
Home saunas are dangerous

claims.claim: Raising core body temperature in early pregnancy is associated with an increased risk of birth defects, so pregnancy is the clearest case for medical advice before heat exposure.

citations.title: Update on the gestational effects of maternal hyperthermia.

claims.hedge: The evidence concerns sustained elevation of maternal core temperature during the first trimester. Pregnant women should be directed to their own clinician, not to a general guideline.
do_not_say: Saunas cause birth defects
Pregnant women must never use a sauna
Sauna is safe during pregnancy

claims.claim: One review of uncomplicated pregnancy concluded sauna bathing did not affect fertility and was tolerated by healthy women, which sits alongside — not above — the hyperthermia evidence.

citations.title: Benefits and risks of sauna bathing.
Update on the gestational effects of maternal hyperthermia.

claims.hedge: These two literatures genuinely disagree in emphasis. The conservative reading governs: core temperature rise in the first trimester is the risk, and this is a decision for the treating clinician.
do_not_say: Sauna is safe in pregnancy
Research shows pregnant women can sauna normally
Sauna does not affect pregnancy

claims.claim: Sauna bathing is generally tolerated by healthy children in the cultures where it is customary, but children heat up faster than adults and need shorter sessions and supervision.

citations.title: Benefits and risks of sauna bathing.
Human thermoregulation in sauna.

claims.hedge: Tolerance in a sauna-bathing culture with customary practice is not a green light for unsupervised use, and thermoregulation differs by body size.
do_not_say: Saunas are safe for kids
Children can use a sauna like adults
